name: Wegener’s continental drift theory
description: Wegener argued that continents had moved and drew together geographical, geological, fossil and climatic evidence.

impact.note: A new picture of moving continents, debated across geology but rejected by most for decades; a few successors kept it alive until other evidence arrived.

date.basis: The cited historical account supports 1912; this is a dated documented episode, not proof of global priority.

events.statement: Wegener introduced his continental drift theory in two articles.

evidence.supports: Wegener’s 1912 articles and the geological, fossil and climate evidence for moving continents.

contributions.resource: Formulated and introduced the continental drift theory in two 1912 articles.

evidence.supports: Attributes 1912 introduction of continental drift theory in two articles to Wegener.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest episode established by the evidence collected here for this scoped achievement, not a claim of absolute priority.

caveats: Others had proposed moving continents earlier. Continental drift is distinct from later plate tectonics and did not supply the later theory’s mechanism.

research.note: New research batch; no independent review claimed. Event contributions, concept, places and extended measure scope were added in a later pass and have not been independently reviewed.
